verdict: P&G grew sales 4% to $23.3B on higher volume and mix, but rising product costs squeezed its gross margin by 160 basis points, leaving net earnings flat at $4.7B — and it warned of roughly $1.9B of commodity, interest and other cost headwinds this year.

segments.name: Fabric & Home Care
segments.note: Tide, Ariel, Dawn and home-care brands — P&G's biggest segment, with 4.3% volume growth.

segments.name: Baby, Feminine & Family Care
segments.note: Pampers, Always and Bounty/Charmin paper products.

segments.name: Beauty
segments.note: Olay, Pantene and SK-II — the fastest-growing segment this quarter.

segments.name: Health Care
segments.note: Crest, Oral-B and Vicks — sales grew even as volumes fell 2.9%, on price and mix.

segments.name: Grooming
segments.note: Gillette and Braun shaving and grooming products.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.note: Corporate items and other small amounts that don't sit in a segment.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, marketing and running the company — down 90 basis points as a share of sales on productivity savings.

otherDetail: Other non-operating income of $207M plus $102M of interest income, less $223M of interest expense, less $26M of profit belonging to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: Other income added $0.26 per $100 of sales after interest and the noncontrolling-interest share. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: Growth was volume-led
takeaways.text: Organic sales rose 4% on a 2% volume increase and 1% favorable mix, with pricing roughly neutral. Every segment grew — Beauty led at +6%.

takeaways.title: Costs squeezed the margin
takeaways.text: Cost of products sold rose 7% — much faster than sales — cutting gross margin from 51.4% to 49.8%. P&G now expects about $1.4B of after-tax commodity cost headwinds in fiscal 2027.

takeaways.title: Cash returns continued
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $5.8B and P&G returned $3.9B to shareowners — $2.6B of dividends and $1.3B of share repurchases. It held its full-year sales and EPS guidance.

oneTimers: Incremental restructuring charges of $98M before tax ($44M in cost of products sold and $54M in SG&A) are excluded from P&G's Core results — the difference between GAAP EPS of $1.97 and Core EPS of $2.00.
footerNote: P&G's lines round $1M apart; other income is shown at $87M (printed components sum to $86M) so the flow balances to reported net earnings.
